answer: Reputation only grows through accepted attestations, so a freshly minted alias starts with zero weight and cannot immediately swing a verdict — the attacker must first spend many epochs building credibility on every single identity. This is resilient because unearned rewards are capped and eventually burned, so an attacker cannot bank on a runaway Sybil campaign paying off. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would.
